newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Rebhold, miners group in 160 mln rand deal.
newsitem.headline: Rebhold, miners group in 160 mln rand deal.

text.p: In a back-to-back deal worth more than 160 million rand, Rebhold Ltd has sold 15 percent of its shares to the Mineworkers Investment Company (MIC) and bought Royal Food Services from the union body and Royal management.
MIC chairman Paul Nkuna said the move was in line with the MIC's plans to build a diversified food and beverage distribution and services group.

"MIC's strategic alliance with Rebhold will enable it to use Rebhold as its empowerment vehicle in relation to its food, beverage and related interests and MIC has granted Rebhold a right of first refusal in relation to certain of MIC's existing invesments in this sector and in relation to all future opportunities in the sector presented to MIC," Nkuna said.

Rebhold chief executive Jacques Kempen said the deal would open new markets for Rebhold while the cash injection "increases the war chest for further acquisitions that we are increasingly being offered".
Royal Foods Services is a supplier of catering services, food services and site and project support services. It has large public and private sector contracts.

Royal's profits have been warranted for 36 months and Rebhold will pay about six times the average annual after-tax profits achieved in the first 24 months through between 9.7 million and 10.2 million Rebhold shares and a maximum of two million rand in cash.

MIC will subscribe for 12 million Rebhold shares at 6.25 rand a share, or a four percent discount. Provided profit warranties on the Royal deal are met, MIC will get further Rebhold shares in exchange for MIC's existing shareholding in Royal.

"The immediate effect of the deal will see an inflow of 75 million rand as additional capital, which puts our cash resources at about 110 million rand and gives further scope for growth," Kempen said.
The deal was not expected to have a material effect on earnings for the year to June 30, 1997.
